Le son numérique a un plafond : 0 dB. To: Digital sound has a ceiling: 0 dB. Anything that tries to go above it gets cut off flat, like a wave being planed off. It makes a harsh crackle you can't remove afterwards.
un son propre, sans craquements, sur tou: a clean sound, with no crackles, on every speaker.
Un mix qu'on va masteriser doit garder d: A mix that's going to be mastered must keep some room under the ceiling, like a glass you don't fill to the brim: aim for peaks between -6 and -3 dB. Mastering is what raises the final volume. If the mix is already maxed out, it has to squash the sound to make it fit.
un mastering qui peut rendre ton morceau: a master that can make your track loud without damaging it.
Tes pics restent sous -3 dB : il reste a: Your peaks stay under -3 dB: there's enough room left for mastering.
Le LUFS mesure le volume tel que ton ore: LUFS measures volume the way your ear feels it, not just the peaks.
Même si chaque point du fichier reste so: Even if every point in the file stays under 0 dB, the real wave coming out of the speakers can go above it between two points. When Spotify or YouTube convert your track (MP3, AAC), these overshoots turn into crackles.
pas de distorsion surprise une fois ton: no surprise distortion once your track is online.
Le PLR, c'est l'écart entre les coups le: PLR is the gap between the loudest hits and the average volume. The smaller it is, the more “squashed” the sound: everything is at the same level, the kicks don't punch anymore, and your ears get tired fast.
des kicks qui frappent et un morceau qu': kicks that hit hard and a track you can listen to for a long time without fatigue.
Ton morceau a beaucoup d'écart entre ses: Your track has a big gap between its loud and quiet moments. That's natural, but in electronic music it can sound less dense, less “big” than other tracks.
(avec un peu de compression) un son plus: (with a bit of compression) a tighter, fuller sound, without squashing it.
La gauche et la droite jouent « à l'enve: Left and right are playing “upside down” from each other. When they're added together (phone, Bluetooth speaker, club sound systems often in mono), they cancel out and sounds disappear.
un morceau qui sonne pareil partout, mêm: a track that sounds the same everywhere, even on a single speaker.
Low sounds should be in the center. In a club, the subwoofer is often mono; a bass spread left and right loses power and gets blurry.
un grave solide et puissant, sur toutes: solid, powerful low end on every sound system.
Un mix où tout est au centre sonne petit: A mix where everything is in the center sounds small and cramped. Width comes from panning (left / right) and from effects like reverb or delay.
de l'espace : chaque son trouve sa place: space: every sound finds its place.
Ton signal est décalé vers le haut ou le: Your signal is shifted up or down instead of being centered on zero. You can't hear it, but it wastes room under the ceiling and can cause little clicks.
headroom you get back for free.
Corriger la piste qui en apporte le plus: Fixing the track that contributes the most is cleaner than fixing the whole mix at once: you only touch what's causing the problem.
un mix plus clair, sans perdre ce qui fa: a clearer mix, without losing what makes the track sound the way it does.
un mix plus complet, qui sonne bien sur: a fuller mix that sounds good on every system.
Quand deux sons jouent dans les mêmes fr: When two sounds play in the same frequencies, your ear can't separate them anymore: they hide each other, like two people talking at the same time. Then you want to turn both up, which makes everything worse. So you make room for one of them. (The analysis looks at the sound on average: if these two sounds never play at the same time, ignore this tip.)
on entend chaque son clairement, sans mo: you hear every sound clearly, without turning up the volume.
Dans Ableton, une piste peut dépasser 0: In Ableton, a track can go above 0 dB without damaging the sound: the internal math has no ceiling. The only real ceiling is the Master output (and the export). But tracks that are too loud push the Master toward clipping and make mixing harder.
des niveaux bien rangés, faciles à mixer: tidy levels, easy to mix, and a Master that doesn't clip.
Cette piste contient des graves qu'on n': This track has low end you can barely hear when it plays alone. But in the mix, these little lows add up with those of the other tracks and muddy the kick and the bass. A gentle low cut removes them. Careful not to set it too high: the track would get thin.
un kick et une basse plus nets, un grave: a clearer kick and bass, a cleaner low end.
Les sons graves doivent être au centre :: Low sounds should be in the center: spread left and right, they lose power, and on a mono sound system (common in clubs) part of them disappears.
un grave plus puissant, qui tient sur to: a more powerful low end that holds up on every sound system.
La gauche et la droite de cette piste s': This track's left and right cancel each other out: played on a single speaker, it will almost disappear. It's often the fault of an effect that widens the sound.
une piste qui reste présente sur télépho: a track that stays present on a phone and in a club.
Le kick et la basse portent l'énergie du: The kick and the bass carry the track's energy. Shifted to one side, the whole track leans over, and on headphones it's annoying.
un morceau équilibré, avec un grave bien: a balanced track, with low end firmly anchored in the center.

Spotify, YouTube et Deezer remettent tou: Spotify, YouTube and Deezer all bring tracks to the same volume, around -14 LUFS (Apple Music around -16). If your track is louder, they turn it down automatically. So mastering very loud doesn't make you louder than the others: you just lose punch. (Many electronic tracks still come out around -9 to -7 LUFS: that's a style choice, not a mistake.)
un morceau qui garde ses coups et sa res: a track that keeps its punch and its breathing on streaming.
En club, personne ne remet les morceaux: In a club, nobody brings tracks to the same volume: the DJ mixes your track with other very loud ones. So electronic tracks for the club are mastered loud (between -9 and -6 LUFS).
